title: Why did people build castles with moats?

lines.text: Movies always show castle moats filled with ferocious man-eating alligators, but why did medieval lords actually build them?
lines.caps: Why did castles *really | have giant water *moats?

lines.text: No, they weren't stocked with crocodiles; they were built to stop the deadliest siege tactic in history: mining.
lines.caps: Built to stop the *deadliest | weapon: underground *mining!

lines.text: Enemy armies didn't just scale walls with ladders; they dug subterranean tunnels straight under castle foundations.
They propped up the tunnels with timber, set them on fire, and collapsed giant stone towers from below.
lines.caps: Setting wooden beams on *fire | collapsed giant stone *towers!

lines.text: A deep moat flooded any underground tunnels with water, drowning enemy diggers instantly.
lines.caps: Moats flooded enemy *tunnels | with tons of *water!

lines.text: Moats also prevented heavy battering rams and rolling siege towers from reaching fortress walls.
lines.caps: Prevented heavy *battering rams | from reaching the *gates

lines.text: A simple ditch of murky water defeated the most advanced medieval siege tactics.
lines.caps: A ditch of murky *water | was the ultimate medieval *defense!
